skill.name: web-search
skill.description: Search the web and extract page content through Tavily and Exa apps exposed by the inference.sh belt CLI.
skill.summary: Run Tavily and Exa web search, answer, and extraction workflows from Claude, Codex, or Claude Code.
skill.author: halt-catch-fire

security_audit.summary: The skill is a legitimate web search and extraction wrapper, but it depends on external CLI execution and third-party services. Most static backtick findings are Markdown false positives, while the real concerns are belt command execution, wildcard belt permissions, remote installs, and disclosure of user queries or extracted content.

remediation.suggestion: Restrict allowed tools to the specific belt app commands used by this skill, or require confirmation for other belt subcommands.
Document that queries, URLs, extracted content, and prompts may be sent to inference.sh, Tavily, Exa, and OpenRouter.
Pin recommended skill or CLI install commands to trusted versions, and avoid encouraging unreviewed additional installs from the skill body.
Use a marketplace-hosted image asset or remove the external image to avoid third-party tracking during rendering.

semantic_findings.title: Broad Belt CLI Permission
semantic_findings.description: The front matter allows `Bash(belt *)`, which permits any belt subcommand, not only the listed search and extraction apps. A prompt could request unintended belt operations within that wildcard scope.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Line 4 explicitly grants wildcard Bash access to the belt CLI. The file later documents multiple belt subcommands, confirming the permission is operational context rather than incidental text.

semantic_findings.title: Third-Party Query and Content Disclosure
semantic_findings.description: The documented workflows send search queries, URLs, extracted page content, and prompts to Tavily, Exa, inference.sh, and OpenRouter. This is expected functionality, but users could expose sensitive research data.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The examples show belt app calls for search, extraction, and OpenRouter Claude models with user-supplied queries, URLs, and prompts. That provides direct evidence of third-party data transfer.

content.value_statement: Research assistants need current sources without manual browsing. This skill runs Tavily and Exa apps through belt for search, extraction, and answers.
actual_capabilities: Runs Tavily Search Assistant queries through the belt CLI.
Extracts clean content and images from URLs with Tavily.
Uses Exa Search to return relevant links with context.
Uses Exa Answer for direct factual responses.
Shows workflows that combine search or extraction with OpenRouter Claude models.
limitations: Requires the inference.sh belt CLI and login before use.
Sends queries, URLs, and content to external services.
Quality depends on Tavily, Exa, OpenRouter, and source availability.
Does not verify extracted claims without additional review.

use_cases.title: Prepare Research Briefs
use_cases.description: Collect current web sources and extract article text for concise briefing notes.

use_cases.title: Build RAG Context
use_cases.description: Gather searchable content from URLs before adding it to retrieval pipelines.

use_cases.title: Track Market Signals
use_cases.description: Compare public sources and summarize trends using search plus LLM workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Web Search
prompt_templates.prompt: Search the web for {topic} with Tavily Search Assistant. Return key sources with short summaries.

prompt_templates.title: Extract Article Content
prompt_templates.prompt: Extract clean text from these URLs: {urls}. Summarize each source and list images when available.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Search Providers
prompt_templates.prompt: Run Tavily Search Assistant and Exa Search for {query}. Compare overlap, unique sources, and source quality.

prompt_templates.title: Build Research Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Search for {topic}, extract the strongest sources, then draft a briefing with citations and open questions.

output_examples.input: Search for privacy risks in browser extensions.
output_examples.output: A concise answer with source links, brief context for each source, and topics that need follow-up review.

output_examples.input: Extract two policy pages and summarize the differences.
output_examples.output: Clean page text, a comparison summary, and a list of claims that require source verification.

output_examples.input: Find recent research on retrieval augmented generation evaluation.
output_examples.output: Relevant links, provider-specific search notes, and a short briefing organized by evaluation theme.

best_practices: Confirm sensitive queries can be shared with Tavily, Exa, inference.sh, and OpenRouter before running commands.
Use specific questions and known domains when source quality matters.
Review returned sources before using answers in reports or agents.
anti_patterns: Do not submit secrets, credentials, or private customer data.
Do not treat AI answers as verified facts without source review.
Do not run broad extraction jobs without checking target site permissions.

faq.question: Does this skill browse the live web?
faq.answer: Yes. It calls Tavily and Exa through the belt CLI when those services are configured.

faq.question: What setup is required?
faq.answer: You need the inference.sh belt CLI, an authenticated session, and access to the listed apps.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. It declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code when belt is available.

faq.question: Can it extract any website?
faq.answer: No. Site access, paywalls, provider limits, and site policies can restrict extraction.

faq.question: Which services receive my data?
faq.answer: Queries and URLs can be sent to inference.sh, Tavily, Exa, and OpenRouter in the documented workflows.

faq.question: Are search answers guaranteed accurate?
faq.answer: No. Review sources and verify important claims before using results in decisions.
